reviews.review: really good graphics still hold up when the rez is turned up to the monitor instead of what it auto sets to

Wanna feel like an invincible Space Marine that slaughters Orks?  Too bad, you'll get this game instead.

I wanna start off by saying this game is not terrible, but it is tedious.  If there was a neutral rating, I would give it that, but Steam doesn't do that.

This is an older game, but it still looks very good and runs well on my aging computer.

The story is fine.  The characters are fine.  The atmosphere is good.  Nothing about the presentation is terrible.

I feel like where this game starts to falter is the combat.  Once you get about 1/3 of the way through the game, you start seeing a lot more Orks with guns, rockets, and mortars.  Your character, the literal Ultramarine, CAN NOT take a lot of damage.  You can no longer wade into battle and start hacking away anymore.  You'll have to hold back and counter-snipe before you can think about diving in.  Otherwise, you will die very easily.

This wouldn't be bad if you played as any one else besides a Space Marine.  Any Space Marine.  Any chapter.  At that point I didn't feel like a Space Marine.  I felt like a random soldier.

The game has zero RPG elements. Maybe you could've had a system to put points into armor and be able to take a lot more damage.  Maybe you could build a sniper class, a melee class, or an assault class, but no.  It's just you and whatever weapons you're carrying.  You do get to choose which guns you carry, but the selection isn't that big.  You can also choose which melee weapon you carry and you can pick the one that fits your style the best.  That's good.  I wanted more of that.

At the end of the day, it's a competently made game, taking place in the Warhammer universe, but doesn't seem to properly convey the experience of being a Space Marine.  That's a problem because the game is called "Space Marine."  I know this game gets a lot of praise heaped onto it, and no one cares about my opinion, but it's a okay game that people want to hold up as a masterpiece.

Even 15 years on, Space Marine is a satisfying and fun gameplay experience, with a brief glimpse into the grim darkness of far future. Witness the origin of Titus (voiced by Mark Strong in 2011), Captain of the Ultramarines' 2nd Company, as you slaughter your way through xenos, daemons and heretics to stem the invasion of the Forge World Graia. Simple yet versatile combat, weighty animations and sound design, a variety of weapon and enemy types to keep you on your toes, and a campaign that doesn't overstay its welcome with additional co-op PvE and PvP modes included.
